title: Large-scale fluid flow shows little sensitive dependence on initial conditions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Large-scale fluid flow shows little sensitive dependence on initial conditions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In almost all cases, large-scale fluid behavior does not depend discernibly on the detailed initial conditions; small perturbations are damped out by viscosity, so sensitive dependence (chaos) is the exception rather than the rule.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: when it comes to large-scale fluid behavior, it seems to be true that in almost all cases there is no discernible difference between what happens with different detailed initial conditions.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Fluid Flow” (from p. 376), p. 381. Scope: large-scale behavior of real and model fluid flows, including turbulence

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Scale-specific perturbation growth is well defined and can be tested computationally in public flow fields. Existing databases cover important but narrow canonical geometries and do not represent almost all real and model flows. Controlled perturbation ensembles may also require new simulations rather than analysis alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For ensembles of nearly identical initial flow fields, track divergence of low-wavenumber velocity and pressure observables while varying viscosity and flow regime. The claim predicts decay or negligible growth of large-scale differences in almost all sampled flows, including turbulent cases.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Large scale and discernible require chosen filters and tolerances.

Almost all cases lacks a sampling distribution over flows.

Single trajectories do not provide controlled pairs of nearby initial conditions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Sensitive dependence of filtered fluid observables is a standard analysis, and public direct numerical simulations contain the fields. Those simulations can refute the claim for the flows they include if large-scale differences grow. They do not inventory almost all flows, and the cutoff between large-scale damping and chaos is itself a modeling choice, so the universal wording stays only partly testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Perturb public velocity fields at small scales and measure the growth or decay of the difference in large-scale observables such as wake spectra and coherent-structure positions. Rapid damping in almost every flow class would support the claim; exponential growth of large-scale differences in typical turbulent flows would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Large-scale and discernible depend on the filter, and predictability time varies by orders of magnitude across flows.

Almost all cases is not represented by the canonical simulations in one database.

operationalizability: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.55
